emails.subject: Your prompt is here (plus a free bonus)
emails.body:
Thanks for grabbing the One-Prompt Website.

Here it is: {SITE}/r/one-prompt-website/

Open a new chat with Claude. Paste the prompt. Answer its questions. About 10 minutes.

Since you're here, take this too. It's free.

The Robot Tells. 12 giveaways that make your writing sound like a machine, and the fix for each: {SITE}/r/robot-tells/

Fix those and the page you just built reads like a person wrote it. Because a person did.

Now the honest part.

The free prompt stops at a free web address. No domain of your own. No way to collect and email the people who sign up.

That's what the One-Chat Launchpad is for. One chat with Claude builds your site, your freebie and your email setup on your own domain. You get the master prompt, a starter template, a click guide and a rollback card.

$19. One time.

{SITE}/launchpad/

Use the free prompt first if you want. The Launchpad will still be there.

Rob

emails.subject: quick question
emails.body:
One question.

What do you actually want help with right now?

Not the polite answer. The real one. The thing you'd ask me if we were sitting at the same table.

Hit reply and tell me in a sentence or two.

I read every reply myself. I'll write back with a straight answer. If it's easier to show than tell, I'll record you a short video instead.

Rob

emails.subject: Did the prompt work?
emails.body:
Quick check. Did you get to run it?

The two places people get stuck:

1. They don't know what to give away. Fix: ask Claude for three options based on your audience's biggest frustration, then pick the one you could finish today.
2. They get stuck at the free hosting step. Fix: tell Claude exactly which screen you're on and what it says. It will walk you through it.

If you're stuck somewhere else, reply and tell me where.

Rob

emails.subject: What the free version leaves out
emails.body:
The free prompt gets you a real page on a free web address. It deliberately stops there.

Three things it leaves out:

1. Your own domain (yourname.com instead of yourname.workers.dev)
2. Collecting and emailing the people who sign up
3. The part where it all connects

I built my own site, two freebies and the email setup in one chat with Claude. The prompt I used, packaged with a starter template, is called the One-Chat Launchpad. I'll tell you what's in it over the next few emails.

Rob

emails.subject: The part that scares beginners
emails.body:
The scary part of owning a website is DNS. That's the setting that connects your domain to your site. Get it wrong and your site, or your email, can stop working.

So the Launchpad has a rule: Claude copies every existing record first, then stops and asks you before it changes anything. It also comes with a one-page Rollback Card that shows how to undo the switch in about two minutes.

You keep control the whole way.

Rob

emails.subject: What's inside the Launchpad
emails.body:
Here's exactly what you get:

- The master prompt that runs the whole build in one chat
- A starter template (the same one this site is built on)
- A click guide listing the few steps only you can do
- The Rollback Card

It's $19, one time: {SITE}/launchpad/

You'll pay a registrar separately for a domain (roughly $10 to $25 a year). Email is a separate add-on.

Who it's for: beginners who want a real site and a lead magnet without hiring anyone.
Who it's not for: anyone who wants a promise of sales. I don't make those, and nobody honest can.

You also need Claude. It works best with a paid plan that has file tools and the Chrome extension. If Claude can't do a step, it walks you through it by hand.

Rob

emails.subject: Last note from me on this
emails.body:
That's the last email about the Launchpad.

If a website and a lead magnet are on your list, the free prompt is yours to keep: {SITE}/r/one-prompt-website/

If you want the full setup, it's here: {SITE}/launchpad/

Either way, I'm glad you grabbed the prompt.

Rob

emails.subject: How's the build going?
emails.body:
Hi {first_name},

Checking in. Where are you in the build?

If your site isn't live on a free address yet, start there. Don't touch the domain until the free address works.

If you're stuck, reply with the stage and what you see.

Rob

emails.subject: When you're ready for email
emails.body:
Hi {first_name},

Once your site is live on your own domain, the next piece is email: sending from your domain, a signup form, and a welcome series.

There's an Email Add-on for that. It has the Stage 6 prompt and 5 welcome-email templates. It's $19: {SITE}/email-addon/

A warning so you don't waste time: email tools often need to approve your account before they send to outside addresses, and that can take a day or more. Start it early.

No rush. Get the site live first.

Rob
